name: AI protein binder design as a service
title: AI protein binder design: is the hit rate a business yet?
question: Is AI-designed protein binders as a service a viable business now?
answer: Computational protein design used to need screening labs because only a small share of designed binders worked. BindCraft, published in Nature in August 2025, reported one-shot designs with high experimental success rates against many targets, without high-throughput screening. The measured crossing is real; the open check is a named, funded graveyard.
verdict_reason: A peer-reviewed crossing exists; no named, funded graveyard yet.

constraint.name: Experimental hit rate of designed binders
constraint.detail: When most designs fail, every project needs a screening facility; when most work, design becomes a service.

crossing.text: BindCraft published in Nature: one-shot binder design with high experimental success.

graveyard_note: Asserted, not enumerated: 'the 2000s-2010s computational drug-design cohort'. Named, funded companies are needed before a ripe call.

evidence.text: Pacesa et al., 'One-shot design of functional protein binders with BindCraft', Nature.
